verdict.reason: Meio da Baia is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

conversationalSummary.text: For TODAY after work (starting around 16:30), Meio da Baia is the best bet but the wind angle is poor, so it can get messy. I’d check the Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam first—if it doesn’t look notably cleaner and more organized than expected, probably skip. If the bay looks like it’s getting that north-northwest push and the waves are actually holding shape as the tide’s rising, then it’s worth a go.

best.explanation: Meio da Baia looks like a fun-sized window for Worth checking, Medium confidence: 0.6-1.1 m, 112 kJ, 8 s period, very consistent 80/100, and wind is the main risk.  An inconsistent Baía spot that can work well when north-northwest swell reaches the bay; this is best for bodyboard sessions when the bay is clean, there is enough period and size, and the forecast shows a defined wave; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot.

Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; 6-9s at mid tide is soft and sectiony on the reef shelves.
